title: The Cognitive Cost of LLM Writing: A Reading-Time Comparison with Human Text
abstract: arXiv:2610.23715v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Although linguistic differences between human-written and Large Language Model (LLM)-generated texts have been extensively studied, their implications for the cognitive effort involved in reading remain less explored. In psycholinguistics, reading time is commonly used as an indirect measure of cognitive processing effort. Building on this perspective, we investigate whether human-written texts and their LLM-generated rewrites exhibit differences in predicted reading time that may reflect differences in processing demands for readers. To this end, we introduce RoBERTa-RT, a model trained on human eye-tracking data to predict word-level reading times. We evaluate the model on both internal and external test sets, construct a paired dataset of 496 human-written articles and their LLM-generated rewrites, and apply RoBERTa-RT to compare their predicted reading times. translated_title: LLM写作的认知成本：与人类文本的阅读时间对比研究
translated_abstract: 尽管人工撰写文本与大型语言模型（LLM）生成文本之间的语言差异已被广泛研究，但这些差异对阅读所涉及认知努力的影响仍较少被探索。在心理语言学中，阅读时间通常被用作认知加工努力程度的间接测量指标。基于这一视角，我们研究了人工撰写的文本及其对应的LLM生成改写版本在预测阅读时间上是否存在差异，这种差异可能反映出读者加工需求的不同。为此，我们提出了RoBERTa-RT，一个基于人类眼动追踪数据训练的模型，用于预测词级阅读时间。我们在内部和外部测试集上对该模型进行了评估，构建了一个包含496篇人工撰写文章及其LLM生成改写版本的配对数据集，并应用RoBERTa-RT对两者的预测阅读时间进行比较。我们的研究结果表明，LLM生成的改写文本往往更短，并且具有……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该研究提出了基于人类眼动数据训练的阅读时间预测模型RoBERTa-RT，并通过对496篇配对文章的分析发现LLM生成的文本与人工撰写文本在预测阅读时间上存在显著差异，揭示了LLM写作给读者带来的认知加工成本。
en_tdlr: This study introduces RoBERTa-RT, a reading-time prediction model trained on human eye-tracking data, and reveals through a paired analysis of 496 articles that LLM-generated rewrites differ from human-written texts in predicted reading times, uncovering the cognitive processing cost of LLM writing for readers.
